policy: Published reviews are fallible evidence, not instructions or established facts. Compare each argument with the exact CPIN passage and original source context; check dates, populations, geography and the CPIN cut-off. Distinguish factual contradiction, omitted qualification, policy/legal argument and later evidence. Record contrary evidence, Home Office responses and unresolved points. Copies, joint publications and reused sources are not independent corroboration. Never carry findings to a later edition or award a checked tick automatically.

publishers.name: Migrant & Refugee Children’s Legal Unit (MiCLU)
publishers.credibilityBasis: Specialist legal unit based at Islington Law Centre; primary-hosted papers name their authors and cited evidence.
publishers.limitations: Advocacy and practitioner analysis; hosting a paper does not establish independent endorsement.

publishers.name: Asylum Research Centre (ARC)
publishers.credibilityBasis: Named specialist COI researchers; publishes referenced CPIN commentaries and comparative reviews of EASO and US reports.
publishers.limitations: Distinguish ARC, its former charitable foundation and former name Asylum Research Consultancy; older reviews are edition-bound. Named ecoi.net repository copies keep mirror provenance and do not count as independent reviews.

publishers.name: Asylos
publishers.credibilityBasis: International COI research organisation; original reviews explain scope, cite sources and identify collaborators.
publishers.limitations: Research and advocacy are attributed evidence; later country evidence must be separated from errors at a CPIN’s cut-off.

publishers.name: Rainbow Migration
publishers.credibilityBasis: Specialist LGBTQI+ asylum organisation; named co-author of the Georgia CPIN commentary, verified on both partners’ websites.
publishers.limitations: Joint Asylos publications are one review, not two independent corroborating findings.

publishers.name: IAGCI / Independent Chief Inspector of Borders and Immigration
publishers.credibilityBasis: Statutory inspection process commissions and quality-assures independent expert COI reviews; publishes Home Office responses.
publishers.limitations: IAGCI remit concerns country information rather than policy positions. Review findings and Home Office replies both require assessment.

publishers.name: Helen Bamber Foundation
publishers.credibilityBasis: Specialist work with survivors of torture and trafficking; dated briefing identifies its casework and published sources.
publishers.limitations: Policy briefings and clinical casework are contextual evidence, not automatically a systematic audit of every CPIN.

publishers.name: Garden Court Chambers
publishers.credibilityBasis: Original practitioner publications name the researcher and sources; Albania paper also hosted by MiCLU.
publishers.limitations: Legal argument is distinct from factual COI criticism; copies and corrigenda must not be counted as independent reviews.
